# Chapter One

She remembered how her grandfather used to spend entire afternoons in the drafty workshop behind the orchard, carefully shaping cedar planks with hand planes until the wood felt as smooth as polished marble. Night came quickly. Cold wind whipped across the vacant harbor as the last ferry disappeared into the gray fog.

Behind the counter, an elderly clerk sorted stacks of yellowed invoices into wooden boxes. Although the city council had promised to repair the crumbling seawall before the winter storms arrived, years of bureaucratic delays and budget disputes had left the concrete barrier vulnerable to the rising tides.
